materials.title: 黃仁勳曾告訴我，那些關於中國與國家安全的問題
materials.text:
黃仁勳曾告訴我，那些關於中國與國家安全的問題
  - Author, 費薩爾·伊斯蘭（Faisal Islam）
  - Role, BBC經濟編輯
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 2 分鐘
Nvidia（輝達／英偉達）行政總裁黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）身上，有一種已故蘋果公司創辦人喬布斯（Steve Jobs）的氣質。我曾分別訪問兩人，他們都有一種近距離接觸時令人難以忽視的個人魅力，以及偶爾流露出帶點鋒芒的天才特質。
兩人都有標誌性的黑色衣着打扮，不過黃仁勳選擇穿皮褸，而非喬布斯那件經典的樽領毛衣。
兩人都是科技界備受推崇的創新者。不過，黃仁勳如今正因涉嫌與一名被指是中國間諜的人士有婚外情受到調查。
過去幾個月，你聽到有關人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI；人工智慧）的所有消息，無論是正面、負面、革命性突破，還是災難性後果，都取決於能否取得最強大的前沿人工智能模型。
而這些模型又有賴最強大的微晶片。多年來，這個領域一直由黃仁勳領導的 Nvidia 主導。公司的技術源自重新改良的遊戲圖像處理技術，並結合台灣強大的晶片製造實力。
Gracehopper、Vera 和 Rubin 等名稱，對一般大眾而言幾乎毫無意義，但它們其實都是晶片的名稱，支援着人工智能模型的開發，而這些模型正改變世界。
去年9月，美國總統特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）訪問英國期間，我曾與黃仁勳會面。當時他正與記者交談，並鼓勵英國繼續發展科技產業。
那次會面也正值他努力游說特朗普解除對華出口限制，讓英偉達可以向中國出售部分性能最強大的人工智能晶片，尤其是H200晶片。
當時，美國已經解除對一款性能較低晶片的出口禁令。我向黃仁勳指出，他是少數能夠走進白宮與特朗普會面，幾天後又能在北京與中國國家主席習近平會面的其中一人。
他毫不掩飾自己的立場，也不避諱表示自己認為已成功說服特朗普接受他的理據。
他說：「特朗普總統的立場非常清楚。他希望美國取得勝利，而習近平主席也希望中國取得勝利，兩者其實可以同時實現。原因是這並不是一場零和遊戲。人類社會的進步，並不是一場零和遊戲。」
他大概是世界上唯一能夠如此有底氣地說出這番話的人，因為他可能曾親耳聽過這兩個超級大國領袖表達各自的想法。
對安全風險的不同看法
然而，黃仁勳所說的「零和遊戲」觀點，並不獲許多國家安全領域的人士認同。
他們認為，爭奪最先進人工智能技術的競賽完全是一場零和遊戲，西方國家、尤其是美國，必須採取關鍵行動，阻止中國取得技術優勢。
他們認為，哪個國家能夠利用最強大的晶片，開發出最強大的人工智能系統，便會在科學發展、破解加密技術、經濟增長，以及網絡武器等領域取得勝利。
黃仁勳則提出另一種看法：這不但不是國家安全挑戰，反而讓全世界、包括中國，都依賴美國的系統，對美國更有利。這些系統被稱為「美國科技堆疊」（American tech stack），而英偉達的晶片正是其中的核心。
黃仁勳更進一步表示，特朗普總統「非常清楚地看待」一個觀點：這類運算技術「並非國家安全問題」。
他告訴我：「任何軍隊都足夠聰明，知道應該以自己的本土技術建立軍事系統，而不是依賴對手來建造自己的技術和軍事能力。」
這反映了甚麼？
當時，也就是如今黃仁勳因國家安全疑慮及涉嫌中國間諜活動而接受獨立調查的同一時期，他公開提出解除對華出口禁令的理據，而且似乎相當清楚特朗普總統的立場。
不止如此，他當時也反駁了另一種說法：中國取得英偉達的技術會構成任何形式的國家安全威脅。
英偉達正處於美國人工智能科技熱潮，以及全球爭奪人工智……

materials.title: 從局長下台到議會「沉默」 宏福苑大火後的政治問責與維穩邏輯
materials.text:
從局長下台到議會「沉默」 香港宏福苑大火後的政治問責與維穩邏輯
香港大埔宏福苑大火慘劇一週年前夕，港府公開獨立委員會的調查報告，點名四個政府部門有缺失。特區行政長官李家超率領官員首次就事件集體鞠躬道歉，房屋局局長何永賢承擔政治責任請辭，其他三名涉事局長繼續留任。
2025年11月發生的這場火災導致168人死亡，1984戶的居民失去家園。
主要官員問責制已推出20多年，外界關注這一波政治問責安排的理據。特首多番強調是其「個人政治決定」，已綜合考慮多個因素。
BBC中文採訪多名政治分析人士，拆解局長請辭如何為問責制建立政治倫理，民間表達與議會監督如何在新政局下被重塑，這場善後操作背後所反映的維穩管治邏輯，以及又與即將舉行的選委會及特首選舉有何深層連結。
問責制源頭與政治倫理
10月29日，中國香港特區政府公開調查火災成因的獨立委員會報告，特首李家超首次就大火率領七名官員鞠躬道歉。
報告點名四個有缺失的政府部門，包括：房屋局獨立審查組（ICU）、屋宇署、消防處及勞工處，它們由四個政策局分別管轄。
就外界關注的政治問責，李家超表示，「政治任命團隊會承擔政治責任」，雖不涉個人犯錯，房屋局長何永賢應承擔政治責任，對方日前已辭職並獲接納。何永賢當日沒有現身記者會道歉，僅發聲明交代「願意為宏福苑的火災承擔政治責任」，當中亦無道歉字句。
主要官員問責制由時任特首董建華在2002年提出，涵蓋並非以公務員條款聘任的政治任命官員，官員或需要為重大政策失誤、執行的嚴重錯失或嚴重的個人操守問題而下台。
曾擔任運輸及房屋局局長的公共行政學者張炳良教授在《明報》撰文指出，政治問責泛指官員因政策失誤、重大社會災難、部屬嚴重疏失或個人醜聞，即使未達違法仍引咎辭職以示負責的制度。
張炳良向BBC中文解釋，問責「無情」，有時候官員毋須犯錯，僅因「on your watch」（在其主政下，或「在眼皮下出現問題」）也要負政治責任。
他說，政治問責沒有絕對做法，也沒有可量化的標準。「有時可能要有人出來承擔責任，令到社會上平息事件，或者用一些人的講法『消消氣』，維護政府的形象，拿回公信力。因為公眾覺得你已負責任，是否很多人要負責任呢？很難講。」
香港主權移交以來歷屆政府當中，有17名在職官員離任，5人請辭，3人以健康理由離任，另有被9人被免職。
2003年，時任保安局局長葉劉淑儀力推23條立法不果，財政司司長梁錦松捲入「偷步買車」風波，二人請辭，前者提及「私人理由」，後者僅交代「現時是我離開的好時機」。
張炳良指出，問責制發展下來，特區未有建立清晰的政治問責倫理，因大部分官員請辭未有交代相關政治原因，其他撤換局長的情況「若因（中國）中央政府或特首覺徥他處理某些事不好，是另一回事，其正式理由也不是問責」，故認為今次房屋局局長直言為火災承擔政治責而請辭，在某程度上屬確立先例。
外界關注北京在香港問責制中的角色，李家超在記者會上被問及決定有否向北京查詢意見、或當局有否「硬指示」，他表示作為行政長官是「第一責任人」及「香港的當家人」，由他作出決定全面考慮。
張炳良則指，不知道中央在宏福苑事件或官員請辭扮演什麼角色，但根據《香港基本法》，一般而言，主要官員由特首提名，中央政府委任。「香港所有司局級官員都是朝廷命官，朝廷就是講『北京』，所以總不能單方面特首說『我要你走』，卻沒有問過委任官員的中央政府，對吧？」
一名局長請辭：有限問責？
政治問責安排的焦點，停留在四個部門被點名，為何只有一名局長要承擔責任，其餘三名涉事局長未有請辭下台。
李家超多番強調，經綜合考慮多個因素，包括官員在事件角色、其政策範圍與事……

materials.title: Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
materials.text:
Poundland hopeful for last-minute rescue deal to stave off collapse
- Published
Poundland and its 11,000 employees are hopeful that the retailer's impending collapse can be delayed to allow time for a last-minute rescue deal.
The discount chain has been edging towards administration after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation have told the BBC that they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of Â£10m in funding.
A committee of MPs is set to question Gordon Brothers, Poundland's US owners, on Wednesday following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal.
Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just Â£1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.
The investment firm has denied the claims.
But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
About Â£50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.

materials.title: Stickers and building sets help drive toy sales ahead of Christmas rush
materials.text:
Stickers and building sets help drive toy sales ahead of Christmas rush
- Published
Traditional games and stickers are helping to drive a bumper year for toy sales, figures show.
The data comes ahead of the crucial Christmas run-in for retailers, which peaks at 23 toys sold every second in the UK.
The number of toys sold up to October was 17% higher than the same period last year and growth is at a 10-year high, according to research company Circana.
The increase comes despite consumers' cost-of-living pressures, and there are signs that some of the biggest growth in sales is for toys priced between Â£5 and Â£10.
Despite relatively low sales in recent years, the toy sector has been buoyed by sales to "kidults".
The kidult market - which is toys and games for those aged over 12 - has been growing, particularly as adults buy toys for themselves.
This growth has continued with a 22% increase in the value of sales in the first half of the year.
But Melissa Symonds, UK toys director at Circana, said that toys for children - which still represents the majority of sales - had recorded a good year so far.
Growing public debate around children's screen time and the role of technology meant squishy toys, stickers and building sets such as Lego were popular.
"Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing that traditional, hands-on play remains overwhelmingly popular," she said.
Concerns have been raised about the suitability of some connected devices.

materials.title: Antidepressant escitalopram more effective at preventing relapse, analysis finds
materials.text:
Antidepressant escitalopram more effective at preventing relapse, analysis finds
- Published
One drug comes out top in a large analysis, external of how effective antidepressants are at keeping patients free of symptoms of depression.
Escitalopram performed best at preventing patients from relapsing in a study involving nearly 10,000 people prescribed different medications for up to a year.
Two other pills - agomelatine and duloxetine - came next, while prozac (also known as fluoxetine) ranked just below them.
Experts stress the findings don't mean that everyone with severe depression should switch to escitalopram, or that other antidepressants aren't any good, because all the drugs can work and each has its pros and cons.
Depression is common, affecting around one in six people in the UK. With the right treatment and support, people can make a good recovery although for some their depression can return.
To prevent relapse, doctors already recommend people stay on antidepressants for at least six months after depression ends, and then taper off gradually.
The new analysis, published in The Lancet Psychiatry, looked at previous studies comparing the effectiveness of more than a dozen common antidepressants in total.
The differences found were modest and experts say longer studies are still needed to find out more.

materials.title: What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?
materials.text:
What's your love language - and does it actually mean anything?
- Published
I'm "words of affirmation", and so is my husband. This is supposedly our shared love language.
But, while we do like receiving compliments, they make us both feel a bit awkward.
Despite this, our result was confidently defined when we took the original Love Languages Quiz online, a personality test published by US pastor Gary Chapman who first came up with the five types of expressing and receiving love in 1992.
I'm sceptical. Does the theory really know more about us than our own lived experience of a 10-year marriage?
The five love languages are: Quality Time, Acts of Service, Words of Affirmation, Receiving Gifts, and Physical Touch - and they feel more ubiquitous than ever.
Contestants on dating shows ask each other their love languages; "My love language isâ¦" is a common prompt on dating apps.
According to the Love Languages website, my husband and I are just two out of more than 150 million people to have taken this particular quiz.
Even though we scored much lower on some of the other languages, they speak more directly to us.
For example I love spending "quality time" with my husband, and feel much more loved by him making lists of films to watch with me than when he pays me a compliment.
But where did the idea of these five neat categories come from? And are they relevant for modern dating and relationships?

materials.title: Robot vessels take on the dangerous work of mine hunting
materials.text:
Robot vessels take on the dangerous work of mine hunting
- Published
Traversing the Strait of Hormuz remains one of the most dangerous trips a vessel can take.
Despite assistance from the US Navy, ships are still being attacked.
"To transit the Strait of Hormuz you need agreement between the captain and the crew to take the risk. You need war risk insurance. And the captain has to make the final decision," says Steve Cameron, a former merchant navy officer and maritime consultant.
Missiles and drones are a threat from the air, but under the surface mines may also be lurking.
"If you're a captain, you'd like to see evidence mines aren't present," Cameron adds.
Modern mines rest on the seabed and detonate when they detect an acoustic or magnetic signal, triggering a pressure wave that will break the keel of a passing vessel.
Others can rise through shallow waters or float, or be powered towards a target.
The technology itself is not difficult or costly, but the mere threat can stop a tanker fleet from sailing.
Ian McFarlane of French defence group Thales is a naval architect who knows mine warfare well. "Mines are a very cheap way of waging a naval war, as the Royal Navy is acutely aware," he says.
Finding sea mines has traditionally been the job of specialist mine-hunting vessels, with crews of around 80 sailors.
To keep humans out of harm's way, an increasing amount of the work is done by systems that are autonomous and monitored from the shore.

materials.title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
materials.text:
Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
- Published
Nvidia has hired one of the largest law firms in the US to investigate the affair between its own chief executive and an alleged Chinese spy.
Jensen Huang, who co-founded the tech company, has admitted to having a romantic relationship outside of his marriage. The woman, Alice Huang, is alleged to be a spy for Beijing.
Nvidia said on Tuesday that it had hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, and that its attorney Joon Kim would lead "a thorough and independent investigation". The FBI is also conducting its own probe.
The company's share price has fallen almost to a yearly low, with $500bn (Â£375bn) wiped of its stock market value since Friday.
Nvidia is widely considered one of the most important companies behind the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, given it is the sole manufacturer of a computer chip used in AI tools.
It is the world's second most valuable company after Apple and its chips have become a matter of national security for US officials who are keen to win the AI race.
Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, and is not related to Jensen Huang, was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has been a customer of Nvidia.
Megaspeed had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia has said was investigated and debunked.

materials.title: The wholehearted life
materials.text:
Listen to this essay
33 minute listen
Six weeks after two open-heart surgeries in 12 days, Roshi Joan Halifax invited me for a visit. She was recovering, but feeling ‘weak as a kitten’. When I’d last seen her, three or four years earlier, her hair had been shorn in a Zen tonsure; now it hung in a lush, grey-streaked braid to the middle of her back. She was pale and short of breath.
As a physician and her friend, I was reluctant to press on with the interview, but she wanted to begin. She was staying with Wendy Lau, her close friend, an emergency physician and Zen priest whose home overlooks Upaya, the Zen centre Halifax established in 1990 in the foothills above Santa Fe in New Mexico. We sat on Lau’s back porch, drinking tea.
Halifax is a medical anthropologist, a Buddhist teacher and a caregiver to the dying, who has worked with the suffering of others for more than 50 years: in burn units and jail clinics, in remote Himalayan villages, at the bedsides of people for whom there was nothing left to cure. She learned that the qualities that drew her there could also pull her under, and more than once they did. When she found her way back, it was Buddhist practice that helped her remain steady enough to help.

materials.title: A trip to upside-down world
materials.text:
For the series Once Upon an Artwork, children are paired with paintings from the collection of the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York City. They’re given free rein to bring their own storytelling and interpretations to the work, and the results are given lively professional animations. In this instalment, two young friends named Dili and Amalia explore I and the Village (1911), a colourful, Cubist-inspired work by the Russian and French Jewish artist Marc Chagall, which draws on his early years in the Hasidic community of Vitebsk, in today’s Belarus. Through the eyes of Dili and Amalia, however, the scene becomes a world where it’s day and night at the same time, memories become visible, everything is upside down and, as such, handstands become a cinch. The resulting short is immersive and playful, serving as a warm reminder of how art inevitably awakens the storyteller inside each of us, no matter our age.

materials.title: 英國美軍在用基地反恐案件：華府稱三伊朗關聯者策劃
materials.text:
英國美軍在用基地反恐案件：華府稱三伊朗關聯者策劃
  - Author, 傑克·伯吉斯（Jack Burgess）
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 3 分鐘
美國司法部宣布已起訴三名獲伊朗支持的行動人員，指他們涉及在美國及歐洲策劃並實施一連串陰謀。
司法部表示，伊朗特工最近曾「策劃一宗針對英國空軍基地的恐怖主義陰謀」，稱他們涉及去年9月發生在英國皇家空軍費爾福德基地（RAF Fairford）附近的「重大事件」，當時美軍駐紮於該基地。
一名擁有伊朗及伊拉克雙重國籍的男子被控在紐約一所監獄中等待就另案受審期間，與英國的聯絡人保持聯繫。另外兩人則被控在伊朗進行同樣活動。
伊朗強烈否認與皇家空軍費爾福德基地事件有任何關聯。該事件曝光時，有人報告在基地附近發現可疑貨車。英國已有七名男子因該事件被捕。
美國司法部表示，伊朗人莫森·莫哈傑里（Mohsen Mohajeri）、伊拉克公民穆罕默德·阿里·哈薩尼（Mohammad Ali al-Hassani），以及擁有伊朗及伊拉克雙重國籍的穆罕默德·巴吉爾·薩德·達烏德·薩迪（Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi），於星期二（11月10日）公開的起訴書中被起訴。
起訴書指控三人策劃在歐洲發動襲擊，並以一個據稱新成立組織的名義實施行動。該組織化名為Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya（HAYI；「右手人民伊斯蘭運動」）。
司法部聲明稱：「2026年春季，HAYI 在歐洲聲稱負責的18宗恐怖襲擊中，有七宗發生在英國。」聲明補充，這些襲擊包括「縱火、爆炸物襲擊，以及一宗在倫敦幾乎致命的持刀襲擊事件，兩名猶太男子遇襲，其中一人擁有美英雙重國籍」。
兩名猶太男子於4月在倫敦北部戈爾德斯格林（Golders Green）遭刺傷。一名疑犯將於明年受審。
美國聯邦調查局（FBI）局長卡什·帕特爾（Kash Patel）表示：「這份包含八項罪名的起訴書顯示，伊朗決心在歐洲及美國發動恐怖襲擊。」
他補充稱，其中一名被告在羈押期間「涉嫌發送加密訊息，以協助未來的暴力行動」。
帕特爾表示，被告涉嫌參與近20宗未遂襲擊，以支持伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊（IRGC）及獲伊朗支持的伊拉克民兵組織真主黨旅（Kataib Hezbollah）。
9月27日，在英國格洛斯特郡（Gloucestershire；告羅士打郡）科茨沃爾德地區（Cotswolds）的皇家空軍費爾福德基地附近，有人發現三輛可疑貨車後，當局宣布進入「重大事件」狀態。
警方未在貨車內發現爆炸物，但檢獲大量汽油。
美國司法部表示，哈薩尼於8月「涉嫌指示並支付英國境內的同夥」，要求他們「為針對皇家空軍費爾福德基地的恐怖主義陰謀進行前期準備及安排後勤」。
司法部稱，8月22日，哈薩尼曾支付一人，要求其「對皇家空軍費爾福德基地週邊進行行動前偵察」。
司法部還指稱，於9月期間，哈薩尼支付多名人士協助其為該陰謀作準備。
根據司法部聲明，相關行動包括「採購貨車及燃料桶、研究購買化學助燃劑，包括大量氯化鉀，以及購買可用作爆炸彈片的金屬物件」。
司法部稱，嫌疑人其後將貨車偽裝成燃料配送公司及泳池用品公司的車輛。
聲明指出：「2026年9月26日，哈薩尼涉嫌指示相關人士駕駛三輛貨車前往皇家空軍費爾福德基地，其中部分貨車其後被確認載有燃料桶。」
司法部還表示，哈薩尼與貨車司機「保持頻繁聯繫」，並協助指示他們行駛路線。
聲明補充：「三輛貨車中至少兩輛在前往皇家空軍費爾福德基地周邊途中，遇到安全路障，未能按照原定路線前進。」
到9月27日……

materials.title: 一名公務員如何長期瞞天過海，身兼五職？
materials.text:
一名公務員如何長期瞞天過海，身兼五職？
  - Author, 佐伊·康威（Zoe Conway）
  - Role, BBC就業記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
2023年5月，阿莉莎·亞當斯（Aleesha Adams）與卡希姆·喬杜里（Kashim Chowdhury）進行視像通話。
當時，喬杜里已因病請假近三個月。他任職於英國衛生安全局（UK Health Security Agency, UKHSA），而身為他的直屬上司，亞當斯希望制定一個計劃，協助他逐步重返工作崗位。
通話一開始，喬杜里便不斷咳嗽，還把紙巾舉到鏡頭前，試圖證明自己病得很重。但真正引起亞當斯注意的，是他看起來異常蒼白。
她留意到，他額頭上的白色粉末開始脫落。她在庭上作供時說：「他一直流汗，那些東西好像被擦掉了，下面的皮膚顏色較深，頸部也是。」
她懷疑喬杜里塗了白色化妝品，刻意扮作病容。他在庭上否認這項指控。
一直未被揭發的欺詐行為
亞當斯當時並不知道，UKHSA並非喬杜里唯一的僱主。
就在同一個月，他還同時受僱於環境、食品及鄉郊事務部（Defra）、商業及貿易部、食品標準局，以及內政部，並且全部都是全職工作。他每星期的合約工時合共達183小時，甚至超過一星期的總時數。他透過欺詐手段，從納稅人手中騙取超過28.4萬英鎊（37.94萬美元；253.27萬元人民幣；1,250.14萬元新台幣）。
2020年至2023年間，他合共曾同時擔任八份互相重疊的公共部門全職工作。這名職級相對初級的公務員在這段期間領取了35萬英鎊薪酬。
與喬杜里通話後不久，亞當斯發現他登入視像會議時，使用的是環境、食品及鄉郊事務部的電郵地址。她向他提出質疑，他卻歸咎於技術故障。
她在倫敦南華克皇家法院（Southwark Crown Court）審訊期間向陪審團表示：「我相信他在說謊。」她隨即向更高層級的主管反映疑慮。
然而，喬杜里的欺詐行為仍然沒有被揭發。他一直能夠同時擔任多份政府工作，直至2023年9月離開公務員體系。
直到2024年，政府的「國家欺詐調查計劃」（National Fraud Initiative）才揭發事件。該計劃每兩年會檢查公務員資料庫尋找異常情況，包括薪酬紀錄。
星期一（11月9日），喬杜里被裁定九項欺詐罪名成立。法官告訴他，他將面臨「非常長的監禁刑期」。
56歲的喬杜里每天獨自到庭應訊。他已婚，但庭上似乎從未有朋友或家人到場支持。
他經常頭戴一頂毛球冷帽，手提兩個塑膠購物袋，沿着法院大樓的走廊走動。
有時，他在證人席上看起來一臉茫然。
喬杜里於2015年被診斷患有創傷後壓力症（PTSD）。他表示，自己之所以接下這麼多工作，是因為過去曾經歷不穩定的就業情況，害怕失去生計。他稱自己在2013年被迫離開教育部的一份工作。
他說當時申請工作時，自己「因為壓力、痛苦和創傷，加上內心恐慌」，未能清晰思考。
但控方反駁指，他的行為是「蓄意」的，屬於「有意欺詐」，並且利用制度漏洞謀取利益。
這宗案件卻也引發公務員體系的重要疑問：他究竟如何能夠長期瞞天過海？
其中一個原因，是公務員體系的人力資源管理系統並非中央統一管理。喬杜里在政府的求職申請表上，沒有申報自己已經是一名公務員，因此系統未能識別重複受聘的情況。
智庫「政府研究所」（Institute for Government）的漢娜·基南（Hannah Keenan）表示，制度顯然失效。
她說：「各政府部門各自獨立作出招聘決定，彼此之間沒有互通資料的系統。」
「不過，這種模式及其背後的文化行不通，其實並不令人意外。我們……

materials.title: Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
materials.text:
Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
- Published
Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (Â£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.
The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month.
It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times.
The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".
It is floating at a volatile time for big tech firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.
There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off.
In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year.
However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn.
Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

materials.title: Sales of tinned food and bottled water  jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
materials.text:
Sales of tinned food and bottled water jump after 'Be Ready' campaign launch
- Published
Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.
Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.
The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.
Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.
"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.
"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in l……

materials.title: Tempted by snacks before bed? Here's why - and what you can do about it
materials.text:
Tempted by snacks before bed? Here's why - and what you can do about it
- Published
You've eaten dinner, you're comfortably full, and yet half an hour later you're raiding the kitchen cupboards. Sound familiar?
Research suggests about a third of people, external are snacking every night after their evening meal - for those aged 18-24, four in five are unable to resist.
Dietitian Dr Kristine Beaulieu says this spells trouble. She points to evidence showing that the more people eat, external within two hours of going to bed, the "greater the odds" of weight gain and obesity.
So, why are evening cravings so common? And what can you do to keep them in check?
Appetite peaks in the evening
Despite the fact we spend longer going without food when we are sleeping, research suggests our appetite naturally peaks in the evening, almost regardless of how much we have eaten earlier in the day.
Prof James Betts, who researches how the body handles food and energy at the University of Bath, says a big factor is that our "hunger hormone" ghrelin is generally higher later in the day.
"While it tends to be suppressed by meals, that really only happens after the first meal of the day, not after lunch or dinner."
But what you eat also matters. Meals rich in protein, fibre and volume tend to keep us satisfied for longer.
Betts says not having a nutritious or satiating evening meal can lead to a "crash" later, which sees people snack.

materials.title: UK doctor infected with Ebola being treated at London hospital
materials.text:
UK doctor infected with Ebola being treated at London hospital
- Published
A British doctor who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown back to the UK.
The man, who has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London.
It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.
Dr Renu Bindra, deputy director of the All Hazards Public Health Response team at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), said there are "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and the risk to the public remains low.
- What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult? 
  - Published15 September
The infected doctor was brought to the UK on a medical evacuation flight as part of a joint effort by the UK and DR Congo governments and their international health partners, the Department of Health (DoH) said.
A convoy of emergency vehicles were on hand to complete the transfer following the man's arrival at the RAF base.
Three large police vans travelled at either end of the convoy, while two ambulances and another support car were involved.
Traffic was stopped and police exited the vans to keep the public away as the convoy arrived at the Royal Free Hospital.

materials.title: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
materials.text:
What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
- Published
One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report.
Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair.
It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company.
Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters.
Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair?
US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown.
Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.

materials.title: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
materials.text:
Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
- Published
Jensen Huang has the air of the late Steve Jobs about him. I have interviewed both, and the up-close charisma - and occasionally scratchy genius - is shared.
Both sported a signature item of black clothing, although Huang opts for a leather jacket rather than the Apple founder's turtle neck.
Both are innovators revered in the tech world. However, Huang is now being investigated over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Everything you have heard about Artificial Intelligence (AI) over the past few months - good, bad, revolutionary and catastrophic - is dependent on having the most powerful frontier AI models.
In turn they depend on the most powerful microchips, and for years that has been this very company, Nvidia, led by Huang, and his technology rooted in repurposed games graphics and the manufacturing prowess of Taiwan.
Names such as Gracehopper, Vera and Rubin mean almost nothing to the public, but are the names of chips powering the creation of AI models transforming the world.
I met Huang as he held court with reporters and offered words of encouragement for the UK's tech future during US President Donald Trump's state visit to the UK in September last year.
It was also right in the middle of his attempts to get Trump to lift export bans to China of some of the highest performing AI chips, specifically the H200.

materials.title: Equality talk
materials.text:
Listen to this essay
36 minute listen
It’s no accident that equality comes first among the ‘self-evident’ truths articulated in the United States Declaration of Independence. The claim that ‘all men are created equal’ serves there not simply as an abstract premise from which revolutionary consequences ought to follow, but as a concrete practical foundation on which the American colonists could claim to stand as equals with the greatest king and hold him to account. Still impressed by his own handiwork 50 years later, Thomas Jefferson even prophesied that the ‘palpable truth’ of equality enshrined in the Declaration would one day unite all of humankind.
Yet today, it’s evident that the word ‘equality’ means very different things to different people. What once seemed capable of providing common ground is now just another source of controversy. What explains this shift? I suspect that the deceptively simple, conceptual language of ‘equality’ has itself played a substantial role. A better understanding of ‘equality talk’ – as the application of this language to human beings and their relations – might therefore shed some light on our predicament.
Let’s begin by examining a group of people that generally prides itself on thinking (and speaking) more clearly than most: professional philosophers. What are they doing when they talk about equality?
Often, they’re saying something about human beings: about what we’re fundamentally like, and how we should be treated morally, politically……

materials.title: Celestial nuisance
materials.text:
Listen to this essay
22 minute listen
In the story of cosmic history, one of the most important supporting characters is dust. As clouds of interstellar gas cooled and condensed in the early Universe, dust grains absorbed and re-emitted radiation, eventually forming stars. Later, dust provided the raw material from which planets could form and grow. Dust grains may even have been the surfaces on which the first complex organic molecules formed. Yet, if you ask most cosmologists, they’ll tell you that dust is a sheer nuisance.
In astrophysics, ‘nuisance’ is a quasi-technical term. Astrophysicists call any phenomenon that gets in the way of the thing they actually want to study a ‘nuisance’. Dust grains emit polarised light that can mimic subtle signals from the afterglow of the Big Bang (the cosmic microwave background) that cosmologists have spent decades and billions of dollars trying to detect. A cosmologist studies dust not to uncover its role in shaping the cosmos, but to subtract it – the term ‘sweeping under the rug’ couldn’t be more apt.
This dichotomy between ‘signal’ and ‘nuisance’ is found across many sub-fields in astronomy. Astronomers who study a phenomenon called ‘weak lensing’ use the subtle distortions of light caused by gravity to map invisible dark matter. For them, the ordinary matter that makes up everything we can see is a nuisance.
